content.text:
The new subcommands are in `bin/todo.js` with tests in `test/cli.test.js`, and `npm test` passes (29 tests, 0 failures). Each test uses a temp dir and `TODO_FILE`, so no real data is touched. I did not edit `src/todo.js` or add any dependencies.

- **`list --tag <tag>`:** filters the sorted list using `list.byTag()`. Tags are lowercased by `src/todo.js`, so `--tag Home` matches `home`. `list` now also shows `(daily)` etc. and `#tags` on each line.
- **`search <query>`:** uses `list.search()`.
- **`done <id>`:** it already existed. I switched it to `completeAndReschedule`, so finishing a recurring item creates the next one and prints `next <id>: due <date>`.
- **`tag <id> <tag>` and `untag <id> <tag>`:** I added these because there was no other way to set tags from the CLI. They call `addTag` and `removeTag`.
- **`export --json`:** prints the raw items as JSON.
- **`export --csv`:** columns are `id,title,done,due,priority,tags,repeat`. Fields containing quotes, commas or newlines are quoted, with `"` doubled. Tags are joined with `;`.
- **`recur <id> <daily|weekly|monthly|none>`:** this one works differently from what you might expect, see below.

The recurrence code that landed in `src/todo.js` has no `setRecurrence`. It has `addRecurring`, which only creates new items, plus `completeAndReschedule` and `nextDue`. Items store `repeat` and `repeatDay`. So `recur` sets or clears those two fields directly in the CLI on an existing item. It refuses items with no due date, because `nextDue` needs one. If the recurrence author later adds a `setRecurrence` method, the CLI should switch to it.

Nothing else is outstanding.
